reading.body:
Microsoft does not publish power capacity, square footage, or individual campus specifications. The company discloses only aggregate worldwide statistics, so this Quincy campus cannot be sized from official sources. Historical local reporting and Microsoft's own community pages confirm it is one of the company's oldest hyperscale sites, dating to around 2007, and part of a multi-county Central Washington region that includes a newer Douglas County facility launched publicly in 2022.

Washington state has 46 mapped data center facilities, but only 2 publish power figures totaling 60 MW. This campus ranks third by published capacity in the state, meaning the ranking reflects other disclosed facilities, not this one. The actual power footprint of the Quincy campus is unknown and cannot be estimated from public data.

For a reader assessing whether this campus matters to AI scaling, the absence of published specifications is the limiting fact. The site's age, Microsoft's scale, and Central Washington's established position as a hyperscale region suggest material significance, but that significance cannot be measured against the grid constraints and compute density that determine AI infrastructure criticality. Without published capacity, this campus remains invisible to quantitative analysis of AI's power demands.
